$comment: BC Transit's eleven transit systems on Vancouver Island, the Gulf Islands and the Sunshine Coast, one feed so the map shows them together, transfers included (docs/DESIGN.md#regions-and-feeds). Published by BC Transit through Consat (tmix.se), an operator id per system (https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/; ids checked 2026-10-28 by downloading each). Every route is drawn; overrides: routes.json. Region: vancouver-island. Terms: https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/terms-of-use/ (identify BC Transit as the source; no use of its marks).
name: BC Transit (Vancouver Island and Sunshine Coast)

static.$comment: Consat exports one system per request (several operatorIds return an empty feed), so fetch-gtfs merges the parts, each its own agency (packages/data/src/gtfs-merge.ts). Their ids are global: the 37 stops two systems share are the same stops (Cowichan Valley's commuter route on Victoria's Douglas St), and the services two share have identical calendars (exports of 2026-10-28); Victoria is first, so its stop names win. The merged feed covers the dates every part does (the earliest end: Nanaimo's 2026-12-19 in the exports of 2026-10-28, against Mount Waddington's 2027-12-31), where its timetable is complete. Each system is regenerated daily with a new feed_version even when its timetable is unchanged, and the export only drops past dates, so fetch-gtfs archives a version only when the merged timetable differs (config/regions/vancouver-island/README.md → Static timetable, OPEN-QUESTIONS #1). calendar_dates.txt only, shape_dist_traveled in metres.

realtime.$comment: No API key and no stated request limit. One request covers every system: the endpoints take several operatorIds (vehicles of 10, 39 and 48 together were the sum of each alone, 2026-10-28). Victoria alone had 185 buses reporting, every one on a trip, fixes p50 ~8 s old when fetched (2026-10-14).
realtime.$poll: Guess, to be polite to a provider that states no limit: positions every 30 s while buses run (05:00-24:00), every 60 s overnight; trip updates (~0.3-1 MB each for every system) every 2 minutes, 5 overnight; alerts every 5 minutes, 15 overnight. About 3,460 requests a day for all eleven systems; dailyCap is a safety net. OPEN-QUESTIONS #2.
realtime.$staleGraceS: Clients fall back to schedule estimates once live data is this much older than the positions poll interval (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$coverageSlackS: Recorder coverage breaks when snapshots are further apart than the positions poll interval plus this (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$interpolateSlackS: Interpolate between two fixes at most the positions poll interval plus this apart (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$extrapolateSlackS: Predict a bus forward for at most the positions poll interval plus this (fixes are fresher than TransLink's: p50 ~8 s, max ~60 s old when fetched in Victoria; guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).

display.$tripId: Trip ids are three internal ids, <journey>:<variant>:<block> (e.g. 11898518:14545024:14591755); the journey alone is unique on any date (Victoria's feed of 2026-10-14: a journey appears in at most two trips, never running the same day). Trip ids are unique across the systems (exports of 2026-10-28).
display.$feedVersion: Versions look like "202610140/20261013 21:00:00/20261014 04:00:00": the export date and a sequence number, then the export window. The merged feed has its newest part's.
